no_shadow_law.rule: If an event payload is not legislated structurally in outbox_events, it SHALL be treated as non-existent by the platform.

invariants.rule: Tickets MUST be issued ONLY after money is confirmed: issuance MUST be triggered solely by ORD-1 order finalization (money-confirmed) and MUST NOT occur on order creation, pending, on_hold, partial payments, or any non-final money state.

Ticket credentials MUST be bearer credentials with a non-PII QR payload; credentials MUST NOT include account identifiers, names, emails, phone numbers, addresses, or any direct personal identifiers; identity linkage SHALL be server-side only.

Admission scope MUST be occurrence-level: occurrence_id is the admission truth key; each credential MUST bind to one-or-more occurrence_id; scanners SHALL enforce EVT-2 admission windows and scan_policy for each occurrence.

Credential lifecycle MUST be explicit and offline-enforceable: any transfer/reissue/rotation/wallet-update SHALL create a new TicketCredential and the prior credential MUST be marked superseded or revoked and MUST fail scanning; supersession MUST be distributed to offline devices via revocation hydration.

Revocations MUST be explainable: TicketRevocation MUST carry reason_subcode referencing ERR-1 registry and a revocation_authority; free-form reasons MUST NOT be used for enforcement decisions or user messaging.

Offline authority is bounded: scanners MUST hydrate signing keys and revocation/supersession sets within EVT-2 max_offline_age_seconds; stale devices MUST deny or validate_only exactly per EVT-2 scan_policy; fail-closed safety is mandatory.

Key rotation MUST be safe for offline operation: credentials MUST carry kid; TKT MUST support active/grace/revoked key states; rotation MUST NOT invalidate valid credentials during an active event lifecycle; compromise SHALL trigger forced reissue and old-kid revocation.

Render artifacts (PDF, wallet passes) MUST be versioned and revocable: artifacts MUST be marked stale on occurrence reschedule and MUST be revoked/superseded on credential revocation/supersession; artifacts MUST be stored as private objects and served via time-limited access tokens.

Wallet passes MUST support issue, update, and revoke with deterministic retry state; failures MUST map to ERR-1 subcodes and SHALL trigger deterministic COMM messaging (COMM-1) and re-download policy.

P0: Each Ticket MUST store checkout_group_id for correlation with multi-org checkout. Ticket.checkout_group_id MUST match the referenced ORD-1 Order.checkout_group_id. Organizer access MUST remain scoped to Ticket.org_id; cross-org checkout MUST NOT weaken tenancy.

P0: Each Ticket MUST reference the immutable price snapshot (pricing_snapshot_id) AND the specific purchased admission line (pricing_line_id) within that snapshot. The pricing_line_id MUST resolve to a PRICE-1 PriceLine in that snapshot; ad-hoc tickets not backed by a signed PricingSnapshot/PriceLine are forbidden.

P0: Admission/redemption truth is occurrence-scoped and owned by SCAN-1. Only SCAN-1 accepted scan attempts MAY advance SCAN-1.RedemptionStatus; validate_only scans MUST NOT mutate RedemptionStatus. TKT-1 MUST NOT create an independent redemption truth store.

P1: Offline verification MUST use two independent mechanisms: (1) TicketCredential QR payload signature for authenticity (anti-forgery), and (2) SCAN-1 signed manifests/policy for eligibility and revocation (anti-replay/anti-reentry). These mechanisms are complementary and MUST NOT be conflated.

P0: Trinity bindings MUST be enforced. Each Ticket MUST bind immutably to: occurrence_id (time/admission scope), pricing_snapshot_id (price snapshot), pricing_line_id (priced item), order_id (money), and checkout_group_id (checkout aggregate). After issuance, these fields MUST NOT change; any correction MUST be expressed via compensating events (e.g., revocation + reissue).

P0: Ticket.status MUST be one of: issued, active, scanned, completed, revoked, expired. issued is the initial state at issuance creation. active indicates the ticket is scan-eligible (payment confirmed AND at least one TicketCredential is available). scanned indicates at least one successful scan/redeem recorded in SCAN-1 for the bound occurrence_id. completed indicates the admission lifecycle is finished as defined by SCAN-1 re-entry/exit policy (if used). revoked indicates the ticket is invalid (e.g., refund/chargeback/admin action) and MUST be rejected by scanners. expired indicates the ticket is no longer valid due to time bounds for the bound occurrence_id. Status transitions MUST be driven by authoritative domain events (ORD-1 payment confirmation, SCAN-1 scan events, REFUND-1 outcomes) and MUST be auditable.

invariants.text: Ticket issuance MUST use an atomic outbox pattern: the Ticket record write and the emission of 'ticketing.ticket.issued.v1' MUST be persisted in the same database transaction. Direct publish to the broker without an outbox is FORBIDDEN.
PII MUST NOT appear in TKT-1 emitted events. Fields such as 'guest_name' (and any other PII in security_posture.pii) MUST be stripped or replaced with reference IDs before publishing events.

notes: If payment plans are supported, contract extension MUST explicitly define issuance thresholds; default is 100% paid.

issuance_trigger.paid_confirmed_at_utc: derived from outbox envelope emitted_at_utc for ticketing.order.finalized.v1 (or PAY confirmation timestamp if present)
issuance_trigger.verified_payment_attempt_id: payment_reference (opaque; MUST reference a verified/final payment attempt per PAY-*)

compromise_handling: On confirmed key compromise, TKT MUST force reissue of affected credentials and mark the compromised kid as revoked.
COMM/fulfillment MUST notify affected holders; offline scanners MUST deny credentials signed by revoked kids after hydration bounds.
distribution_requirements: Scanner hydration MUST include public keys for all active and grace kids relevant to the event lifecycle.
Grace keys MUST remain verifiable at least until the associated occurrence has ended (EVT-2 end time).
Grace overlap MUST be > EVT-2.occurrence.scan_max_offline_age_seconds, per SEC-1.key_lifecycle.grace_window_seconds.
Any offline snapshot_valid_until_utc MUST be <= snapshot_at_utc + EVT-2.occurrence.scan_max_offline_age_seconds (SEC-1 enforced).

kid_semantics.must: kid MUST be treated as an opaque identifier; allowed format and epoch semantics are governed by SEC-1.key_lifecycle (kid_format + epoch). Implementations MUST NOT embed or parse epochs inside kid strings unless explicitly mandated by SEC-1.

issuance_latency_budget_ms.notes: Includes async render; admission validation must not rely on render completion.

Scan evidence semantics and dedupe/conflict concepts (scanner side).
Canonical error envelope + subcode registry referenced by issuance/validation outcomes.
PII vaulting and tokenization boundary; tickets/QR MUST be PII-free.
Cryptoshred + DSAR handling for linkability without deleting immutable truth.
Observability + redaction + trace_id requirements; no raw credential payload logging.
Async job taxonomy used for issuance rendering, wallet ops, and revocation propagation.
Idempotency + lock ordering for issuance and transfer workflows.
UUIDv7 + utc_datetime_usec patterns and naming conventions.
JSON Canonicalization Scheme for signing and verification inputs.

observability.trace_propagation: trace_id MUST be carried through issuance and wallet jobs; logs MUST redact credential payloads and wallet tokens.

notes: This contract defines slot production rules only. The hydration manifest assembler MUST comply with SEC-1 ordering + signature rules.
Any divergence in dedup/sort rules is a P0 split-brain risk for offline scanners.

owned_slots.description: Populate SEC-1 OfflineHydrationPayloadV1.{revoked_ticket_credential_ids,superseded_ticket_credential_ids} for a given org_id + occurrence_id snapshot.

revoked_ticket_credential_ids.dominance_rule: If a credential_id appears in superseded_ticket_credential_ids for the snapshot, it MUST NOT also appear in revoked_ticket_credential_ids (supersede dominates).

ordering.must: Arrays MUST be de-duplicated and sorted lexicographically ascending prior to signing the manifest.

snapshot_cutoff.rule: Only include items with their effective timestamp <= snapshot_at_utc.

notes: Superseded credentials MUST be treated as revoked for scan decisions.
Future optimization (Bloom filter) is permitted only if false-positives fail-closed and are bounded by policy.

outbox_events.notes: Emitted exactly once when a ticket reaches status=issued and the initial credential is minted. MUST be atomic with ticket persistence.
Emitted when a credential is superseded by a newly minted credential for the same ticket. Old credential remains revoked/invalid for admission.
Emitted when a credential is revoked and MUST be treated as final for admission decisions (deny).
Emitted when a render artifact is generated (PDF/PKPASS/etc). Payload MUST NOT include URLs; use sha256/bytes for audit.
Emitted when an existing render artifact is marked stale and MUST be regenerated before distribution.
Emitted when a wallet binding update is queued/requested for external wallet providers.
Emitted when a wallet binding is revoked and the pass MUST be considered invalid.
Emitted when an abuse signal is recorded for enforcement/analytics. MUST be pseudonymous (no PII).

does_not_own: Order pricing and checkout finalization (ORD-1, PRICE-1).
Seat map modeling and inventory truth (SEAT-1).
Scanner device sessioning and scan event reconciliation (SCAN-1).
PII vault storage (PII-1) or DSAR orchestration (DSAR-1).
purpose_and_boundaries.notes:
- Redemption/admission state for occurrences is owned by SCAN-1 (ScanAttemptLog + RedemptionStatus). TKT-1 MUST NOT invent an independent redemption truth store.
- PII mapping for ticket buyer identity is out of scope for TKT-1 and MUST be held in a dedicated PII/PCI boundary (future contract), not inside Ticket or TicketCredential.
owns: Ticket records (access entitlements) scoped to org_id and bound to finalized/paid orders.
Credential issuance lifecycle and revocation/supersession semantics.
Template constraints and render artifact integrity references (hashes, not blobs).
purpose_and_boundaries.purpose: Provide an authoritative, enforceable definition of what a ticket is, when it may be issued, and how its credentials (QR/wallet) are generated, verified, transferred, and revoked without embedding PII.

reschedule_policy: On EVT-2 occurrence reschedule, related artifacts MUST be marked stale and regenerated; credential identity MUST NOT change unless the occurrence_id binding changes.
storage_policy: Artifacts MUST be stored as private objects.
Artifacts MUST be served via time-limited access tokens; public CDN URLs MUST NOT be the source of truth.

must: The platform MUST record a TicketAbuseSignal for every denied scan decision and for any allow_with_notice decision (see SCAN-1).
TicketAbuseSignal MUST be linkable to actor_id server-side (via ticket ownership/transfer resolution) but MUST NOT require embedding identity in the QR claims.
Repeated abuse signals MUST be eligible for downstream sanctions (suspension/ban) owned by IAM-1 policy configuration.
notes: This is a pseudonymous enforcement trail: keep it minimal, auditable, and DSAR/PII compliant.

must: The canonical QR payload format is TKT-CRED-V1 as defined in credential_envelope.
Credentials MUST carry kid and MUST be signed with Ed25519 (EdDSA).
Claims MUST include occurrence_id and time bounds (iat_utc, nbf_utc, exp_utc).
Claims MUST NOT contain PII or durable identity.
notes: Human-readable ticket labels (order number, name) may exist in the PDF/pass UI layer, but MUST NOT be part of the signed QR claims.

must: Issuance MUST be triggered only by ORD-1 ticketing.order.finalized.v1 (money-confirmed).
Issuance MUST NOT occur for pending, on_hold, awaiting_manual_verification, payment_plan_partial, failed, or canceled orders.
If payment plans exist, issuance_threshold MUST default to 100% paid unless an explicit contract extension overrides it.
notes: This boundary is the irreversible seam: once issued, credentials are bearer instruments and must be revocable/supersedable.

must: Render artifacts MUST be versioned and can be stale/revoked/failed.
Artifacts MUST be stored privately and served via time-limited tokens.
On occurrence reschedule, artifacts MUST be marked stale and regenerated; wallet updates MUST be enqueued where bound.
notes: Artifacts are not the 'truth'; the signed credential + revocation state is.

must: The QR is a bearer credential; replay/sharing is mitigated by SCAN-1 evidence, scan intents, and EVT-2 scan_policy (e.g., anti-passback).
Supersession and revocation MUST be enforceable offline via SCAN-1 hydration payloads that include revocation/supersession state for the occurrence(s) (owned by SCAN-1; referenced here).
notes: Do NOT embed account identity in the credential to 'solve enforcement'—it breaks PII posture and increases sharing attack surface.
Screenshots are still bearer-presentations; anti-passback and anomaly signals are the primary mitigations unless a future dynamic-barcode extension is adopted.

must: Wallet bindings MUST track provider, external_pass_id, lifecycle status, last_attempt_at_utc, attempt_count, and last_error_subcode.
Wallet update/revoke retries MUST be bounded; failures MUST map to ERR-1 subcodes.
notes: Wallet binding is operational state; it MUST survive retries and be auditable.

anti_abuse.rule: Repeat-offender tracking MUST be pseudonymous; enforcement actions (warnings, suspensions, bans) MUST be capability-gated and auditable.

credential_signing.payload_policy: Signed payload MUST include org_id, ticket_id, credential_id, and a nonce/issue_epoch; MUST NOT include PII.

pii.rule: Ticket and credential payloads MUST be PII-free. Any mapping to email/phone/name occurs only via PII-1 vault tokens.

summary:
Defines the authoritative, PII-free issuance, lifecycle, transfer, and revocation rules for event tickets and their scannable credentials (QR/wallet) in a strict multi-tenant suite.

v1.5.0: Structural Sovereignty (No Shadow Law) — authoritative outbox_events legislated; PII-1/DATA-1/PROD-1/GOV-0 alignment.

notes: Template theming is controlled; layout remains deterministic and policy-limited to avoid HTML chaos.

title: Ticket Issuance, Credentials, Rendering, and Wallet Bindings

failure_policy: Failures MUST be recorded with ERR-1 subcodes and bounded retry counters.
Failure to update MUST trigger deterministic user messaging (COMM-1) and re-download policy.
